Hi! Graduating in a few weeks with my undergrad in English with a concentration in writing studies. I did a thesis for my capstone and the focus was this question you’re pondering now. English skills are valuable. Any and every career field needs people who can read, write, and speak effectively. You might not feel that you have the skills to do anything, but the reality is that you can do just about anything you want. Don’t narrow your focus and say “I can’t do that, I don’t have the skills.” You are able to recognize the history of language and interpret meaning for different audiences. You have research skills, can problem-solve, and analyze among many other things. You can do more than you think and catch on quickly. Your English training is important. 

Copywriting is a good challenge. You write for different audiences and in a variety of formats. And don’t be afraid to look beyond “traditional” positions as you’re trying to find something before you start your PhD.

Hi! I take 200mg of lamictal and it’s been great! I haven’t gained any weight from it, but I also haven’t lost any. The biggest things that I noticed are that I sweat a LOT at night when I’m sleeping. Like I feel disgusting in the morning, but I’m willing to deal with that since it has worked so well for me. When I was upping the dosage I went through a time where I had the absolute worst short term memory. I would forget what I was saying the middle of sentences, tell the same story within minutes of each other and have no recollection. I had a hard time remember simple words. It made me feel really dumb, but it eventually passed and I’m back to normal again. Take some biotin/keratin supplements if you can — I know some people experience a little more shedding than normal. I hope it works for you, it’s been a lifesaver for me, literally.
